key_insight: Linking atomistic NiAl stiffness to EBSD-informed finite element models predicts polycrystalline elastic properties in very good agreement with experiments.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports microstructure-aware prediction of NiAl stiffness while accounting for grain orientations, sizes and morphology.
method: Compute single-crystal NiAl stiffness tensors using atomistic calculations.
Build a 3D polycrystal from EBSD-derived grain orientation and size distributions, then simulate uniaxial tension with FEM.
Compare effective elastic properties with experiments and analytical homogenization estimates.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports very good numerical–experimental agreement for Young’s modulus and Poisson’s ratio; the Hashin–Shtrikman upper bound and self-consistent approximation closely reproduce experimental Young’s modulus.
watch_item: Agreement depends on the stated model assumptions; the abstract provides no numerical error metrics or validation beyond elastic response.
paper_title: Multiscale evaluation of the elastic response of polycrystalline NiAl using molecular statics, EBSD-based finite element and analytical homogenization methods
